subject: Convert GRASS RGB colour ramp to ggplot2 colour scale

messages.author: 2742e3f54c1ed006
messages.subject: Convert GRASS RGB colour ramp to ggplot2 colour scale
parts:
I am not really thinking clearly on this. The 'terrain' colour scale as
documented in the GRASS source
(https://svn.osgeo.org/grass/grass/branches/releasebranch_6_4/lib/gis/colors/)
is a set of discrete elevation values assigned RGB colour values as
shown below. How can I convert these to a fill scale for use with
ggplot's scale_fill_manual or similar?

In particular, I want to colour a DEM using geom_raster with the
'terrain' colour ramp:

ggplot() + theme_bw() + coord_fixed() +
geom_raster(my.DEM.df, aes(long, lat, fill=ELEVATION)) +
scale_fill_manual(values=??, limits=??, breaks=??, na.value="white")

The terrain colour ramp has fixed breaks, meaning I suppose that similar
elevations in any derived map will be the same colour. That's fine with
me, but also curious to know how I might scale it to fit in with the
elevation range of my DEM.

# 'terrain' colour ramp:
# [ELEVATION R G B]
-11000 0 0 0
-500 0 0 30
-100 0 0 200
-1 150 150 255
0 0 120 0
100 0 150 0
270 90 165 90
300 90 175 90
500 50 180 50
500 70 170 70
1000 70 145 75
1000 70 155 75
2000 150 156 100
2800 220 220 220
3000 255 255 255
8850 255 255 255
nv white

messages.subject: Re: Convert GRASS RGB colour ramp to ggplot2 colour scale
parts:
I made a function a while ago that takes RGB and makes Lab LCH XYZ and RGBHex values from them. You can plot the colors using scale_*_identity(), where * is fill or colour depending on need and geom. 

Usage would be like:

my.DEM.df2 <- RGB2All(data=my.DEM.df, R="R", G="G", B="B", name.ext="", deg.obs=2, illum="C")
ggplot() + theme_bw() + coord_fixed() +

geom_raster(my.DEM.df2, aes(long, lat, fill=Hex)) +
  scale_fill_identity(na.value="white")

You might have to fix it a bit because you didn't supply a reproducible example (i.e. dput()), but this should plot the color of your object as called for in RGB. 

Alternatively, 

require(plyr)
df<-data.frame(R=c(0,128,255), G=c(0,128,255), B=c(0,128,255))

df<-ddply(df, 1, transform, Hex=rgb(R/255,G/255,B/255))

df
#    R   G   B     Hex
#1   0   0   0 #000000
#2 128 128 128 #808080
#3 255 255 255 #FFFFFF

B
